title: Voting for an unvalidated emergency spell costs an Aligned Delegate recognition and their entire bonded buffer
content:
A.1.10.5.2.3.3.2 and A.1.10.5.3.2.3.2 attach the same penalty to the same failure: "It is severe misalignment for an Aligned Delegate to vote for a Standby Spell [or an Emergency Drop Spell] whose authenticity has not been validated... Aligned Delegates in breach of this requirement must be immediately derecognized and their full AD Buffer should be confiscated."

The penalty is what makes the verification duty in A.1.10.5.2.3.3 real rather than aspirational. A procedural checklist that costs nothing to skip will be skipped under time pressure, especially when skipping it looks like helpfulness — voting fast to save the protocol. Pricing the shortcut at the delegate's entire bonded capital plus their standing inverts that incentive.

Two design details are deliberate. First, there is **no proportionality**: the whole buffer, not a slice sized to the harm. Second, the trigger is procedural, not consequential — the breach is voting without validation, whether or not the spell turned out to be genuine. A delegate who waves through an authentic spell without checking is in full breach, because the offence is destroying the verification layer, not causing a loss.

A.1.10.5.2.4 and A.1.10.5.3.3 generalize the stance: breach of *any* requirement concerning Emergency Spells constitutes misalignment and must be addressed under the emergency-preparedness accountability process.
description: Named as severe misalignment with a fixed consequence: immediate derecognition and confiscation of the full AD Buffer — no proportionality, no discretion over the amount.
